config.prompt: Four phases, one audit — put the LCA architecture in order:
items: Goal and scope: what question, what boundaries, what functional unit
Inventory analysis: every flow of energy, material, water and emission
Impact assessment: inventory lines characterised into categories like CO₂-e
Interpretation: sensitivity and uncertainty analysis — which assumptions move the answer
config.why: The functional unit is the secret weapon: comparisons are meaningless until the service is defined — a cup vs 1,000 served drinks can crown different winners from the same inventory.

activities.anchor: The GWP horizon choice (20 vs 100 years) is not pedantry
activities.caption: call the conversion — methane into the common currency
activities.name: smlGwpEstimate

config.prompt: Characterisation: one tonne of methane, counted over a 100-year frame, becomes how many tonnes of CO₂-e?
config.why: ≈ 28 (AR5; ~27–30 in AR6). Counted over two decades the factor is ~80 — methane is strong but short-lived, ~12 years of residence.
config.context: The horizon somebody has to choose is a value choice — the technical debate behind GWP* and livestock accounting.

activities.anchor: Reusable packaging is the canonical trade-off case
activities.caption: file each classic finding by its lesson
activities.name: smlClassicBuckets

config.prompt: The classic findings each teach a different lesson — file them:

items.label: cotton tote vs plastic bag — ~130+ reuses
ceramic mug vs paper cup — 20–100 washes
EV on a coal-heavy grid: break-even ~60,000–90,000 km; on a clean grid ~20,000
beef ~60 kg CO₂-e/kg vs ~6 chicken vs ~1 legumes
transport is only ~10% of food emissions

config.why: The meta-lesson of all four cases: the use phase and the system context dominate — exactly what boundary-drawing is designed to catch.

activities.anchor: before a single delivery van moves
activities.caption: bet before you read on — the bigger lever
activities.name: smlFoodMilesPredict

config.q: You want to shrink one meal's climate footprint. Which move does more?
choices: Choosing the local-farm version of the same beef
They come out about the same
config.why: Transport is ~10% of food emissions; beef carries roughly sixty times the footprint per kilogram of legumes — one swapped meal outweighs a year of choosing the nearer supermarket.

activities.anchor: Scaled to organisations, the standard is
activities.caption: pair each metric with what it actually counts
activities.name: smlScopeMatch

config.prompt: The accounting ledger, from stacks to value chain — pair them:

pairs.right: direct emissions from the company's own stacks
everything up and down the value chain — often 70–90% of a product company's total
what a country emits within its borders
what its residents cause, wherever emitted — the distinction that reveals offshoring

config.why: Scope 3 is usually the largest and the least controlled, and roughly 20–25% of global CO₂ is offshored — which is why disclosure regimes and consumption footprints matter.

activities.anchor: so a nation can shrink its own number by closing steelworks
activities.caption: territorial emissions fell — audit before celebrating
activities.name: smlLedgerBranch

config.root: A country reports falling production-based emissions over a decade. You are the auditor.

start.text: What is the first question to ask?

choices.label: Did heavy industry close, with imports replacing it?
Did emissions fall while the economy grew — real efficiency, or rebound and leakage?
No question needed — the number fell
choices.feedback: The auditor's reflex should fire here.

offshore.text: Then the emissions reappear in the exporter's ledger — roughly 20–25% of global CO₂ moves this way; consumption-based footprints are the honest gauge.

decouple.text: 30+ countries show absolute decoupling — the EU's emissions fell ~30% since 1990 while its economy grew. Check the two caveats: the rebound effect and consumption-based leakage.

naive.text: Production-based accounting counts only what is emitted inside the borders — the number can fall while the footprint does not.

config.why: A territorial account can shrink by closing heavy plant and importing the product — the honest gauge of who is actually causing what is consumption-based.

activities.caption: fill the blanks — the planetary gauge panel
activities.name: smlBoundariesCloze

config.text: The planetary-boundaries panel sets %%0%% Earth-system limits. The 2023 assessment found %%1%% of them crossed — all but ocean acidification, atmospheric aerosol loading and stratospheric ozone, and ozone is the one the %%2%% pulled back.
config.hint: Boundaries are context gauges for the planet, not management targets for a firm.

activities.anchor: Recycling is not a virtue in itself
activities.caption: put glass on the remelt-energy scale
activities.name: smlRecyclePlace

config.prompt: Remelting aluminium takes ~5% of the smelting-from-bauxite energy; steel ~25–30%. Where does glass sit on this scale?
config.why: Glass ~60–70% — the melting energy dominates either way. Paper saves ~40% but costs fibre length each cycle: 5–7 loops before virgin fibre must re-enter.
